procedural_matters: The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
facts: The conditions at the time of the incident were wind of 15 to 20 knots and choppy sea state.
Halfway up the first upwind leg, DEN 2734 was sailing on a close-hauled course on port tack.
DEN 3174 was reaching, coming downwind in another fleet on also sailing on port tack.
DEN 3174 luffed, lost control of the boat and heeled to leeward.
There was contact between the top of the sail of DEN 3174 and the middle shroud on the port side of DEN 2734.
It took approximately one minute to untangle and upright the boat of DEN 2734.
DEN 3174 took a one turn penalty and retired from the race.
DEN 2734 was in last place after uprighting the boat.
There was no damage or injury to either boat.
conclusions: DEN 3174 to windward failed to keep clear of DEN 2734 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
DEN 3174 did not avoid contact with DEN 2734 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a)
It was not reasonably possible for DEN 2734 the right-of-way boat to avoid contact with DEN 3174 when it became clear that DEN 3174 was not keeping clear.
NOR 12.1 states that for 29ers RRS 44.1(b) is changed to a One-Turn Penalty.
By taking a One-Turn Penalty DEN 3174 took an applicable penalty as required by NOR 12.1.
DEN 2734’s place in race 6 was made significantly worse through no fault of her own because of the action of DEN 3174 that was breaking RRS 11 and 14, and she took the appropriate penalty.
However, there was no damage or injury.
Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(2) are not met.
